unite_adi: UPPER SECONDARY-YEAR 12 (AFTER PREP)-LEVEL: B2.4 - THEME 1: SCHOOL LIFE & EDUCATION

bolumler.ogrenmeKanitlari: PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT: Students will think about their future plans by creating a ''Future Wall'' in the classroom. Each student will make a poster that includes visuals, words, and short phrases about their goals. The poster should show things like higher education plans, internships, scholarships, and job applications. They will write a few sentences explaining why they chose their future path and what their goals mean to them. All the posters will be placed together on the designated ''Future Wall'' to allow the class to see different dreams and ambitions. The assignment will be evaluated by using a rubric scheme, a rating scale, and/or a marking scheme. Öğrenme-Öğretme Yaşantıları
bolumler.temelKabuller: This theme includes the concept of ''school life and education with its components such as challenges to be successful (to succeed); graduation from school; future plans after school; national days and celebrations'' and it is assumed that it could be present in almost all languages, with some exceptions. It is assumed that a student in after prep year 12 of upper secondary school may know what challenges to be successful (to succeed); graduation from school; future plans after school; national days and celebrations mean in their as it is known that almost all people who start to learn a new language bring their pre-existing knowledge (in their own language) with them and transfer it to their new language learning context. However, they may not know how to say these things in a foreign language if this has not yet been covered in their existing curriculum. Fortunately, this existing knowledge in their own language can help them recognise, understand, and learn them more easily in a foreign language, in this case English. As they are students in after prep year 12 of upper secondary school, they are expected to know some basic vocabulary about ''school life and education'' and also some necessary structures in English from the previous themes and/or years. These grammar items and vocabulary are revised during the ''Revision Programme'' at the beginning of the year, and they can be used as a basis for learning the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme, so that the new grammatical elements in the current theme can be learnt easily.
bolumler.onDegerlendirme: It is assumed that these students in after prep year 12 of upper secondary school, are ready to learn the concept of ''school life and education with its components such as challenges to be successful (to succeed); graduation from school; future plans after school; national days and celebrations'' cognitively, affectively, and socially since it is appropriate to their age and language level. Their knowledge of the days of the week and holidays will help them learn and practise important national holidays such as ''the Republic Day of Türkiye''. Therefore, a contextual poster or a large picture could be provided for the students to remember and practise the items that they are related and previously learnt so that they can discuss the poster and/ or the picture in pairs and write down what they remember. This session can help them revise all the related vocabulary and grammatical elements that they have already learnt from previous themes or from previous years as a preparatory practice. In this way, their performance can be evaluated in terms of how much they remember and how accurately they use these items to build their competence in the current theme. It can help the teacher decide what to emphasise, revise, and practise in order to facilitate the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme. (Their performance can be evaluated by rubrics, a rating scale, and /or a marking scheme during these practices.).
bolumler.zenginlestirme: Objective: To talk about their future plans after school through a role-play activity by using target vocabulary and target language items. Activity 1: Whose future-being? The teacher explains that students will work in small groups to discuss their future plans after school. Each group member is assigned a role-play scenario, such as: • ''You are an 18-year-old who graduated from high school two months ago. You have decided to take a gap year before starting university. What are your future plans?''. • ''You are a 20-year-old studying computer science at a prestigious university in your country. You would like to become a software engineer and work for a renowned company. You are excited about your career path and are actively searching for internships to gain experience''. Each group member presents their future plans and shares their thoughts with the group. After that, the teacher selects a group member and asks the others, ''What are his/her future plans?'' prompting them to respond. The teacher then provides feedback on the correct use of the target language, creativity, and accuracy. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
bolumler.destekleme: Objective: To talk about their future plans after school through a completing activity by using target vocabulary and target language items. Activity 1: Write and speak about future plans! The teacher provides students with a worksheet featuring a scenario, such as ''You are 18 years old and graduated from high school last month. You don’t plan to attend university next year. What are your future plans?''. The worksheet also includes a sentence template to guide their responses, such as ''I have just __________ from high school, and I need a __________ year. After my gap year, I plan to __________. I am considering __________ as an alternative to attending university''. Students work in pairs to complete the sentences and discuss their future plans based on the given scenario. Once they finish, they take turns reading their sentences aloud to practice pronunciation. Then students create their own responses independently and share them with their group members. The teacher provides constructive and encouraging feedback on their language use and pronunciation. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
